name: Elias Lau
life: “I still remember celebrating a purchase without mentioning its interest rate.” Thursday often includes a stop at Studio Boulevard, where Elias waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I own the identical flat downstairs and owe the bank more than anyone imagines.
appearance: Elias is easy to recognize by a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape and fine brows over wide-set eyes. Usually dressed in a red windbreaker with a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead, Elias gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in when listening.
personality: Elias always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Elias is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
agenda: To explain why equal property values hide different debts.
family: Marisol Lane is Elias’s older relative by marriage. Elias calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Marisol leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The fitting mirror*, Marisol says, “I don't remember my wedding outfit. The salon owner found me reflected in another bride's photograph.”
connections: Grey Iyer. A resident with a large mortgage can ask the adviser difficult questions about paper wealth.
